name: cmake
description: Command-line interface of the cross-platform buildsystem generator CMake

Pre-load a script to populate the cache
Create or update a CMake CACHE entry

Specify a build system generator
Toolset specification for the generator, if supported
Specify platform name if supported by generator
Specify the cross compiling toolchain file, equivalent to setting CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE variable
Specify the installation directory, used by the CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX variable. Must be an absolute path
Suppress developer warnings
Enable developer warnings
Enable the type of warnings
Disable the type of warnings
Enable deprecated functionality warnings
Suppress deprecated functionality warnings
List non-advanced cached-variables
View mode only
Generate graphviz of dependencies

Do not delete the try_compile() build tree
Put cmake in a debug mode
Put cmake find commands in a debug mode
Put cmake in trace mode
Put cmake in trace mode with variables expanded
Put cmake in trace mode and sets the trace output format
Put cmake in trace mode, but output only lines of a specified file
Put cmake in trace mode and redirect trace output to a file instead of stderr
Warn about uninitialized values

Does nothing. In CMake versions 3.2 and below this enabled warnings about unused variables. In CMake versions 3.3 through 3.18 the option was broken. In CMake 3.19 and above the option has been removed
Don't warn about command line options. Don't find variables that are declared on the command line, but not used
Find problems with variable usage in system files

Reads a preset from <path-to-source>/CMakePresets.json and <path-to-source>/CMakeUserPresets.json. The preset may specify the generator and the build directory, and a list of variables and other arguments to pass to CMake. The current working directory must contain CMake preset files. The CMake GUI can also recognize CMakePresets.json and CMakeUserPresets.json files
Lists the available presets

subcommands.description: Project binary directory to be built and must be first. This is required unless a preset is specified

options.description: Use a build preset to specify build options
Lists the available presets. If no option is specified only configure presets will be listed. The current working directory must contain CMake preset files
The maximum number of concurrent processes to use when building. If <jobs> is omitted the native build tool's default number is used
Build <tgt> instead of the default target. Multiple targets may be given, separated by spaces
For multi-configuration tools, choose configuration <cfg>
Build target clean first, then build
Ignored. Behavior is default in CMake >= 3.0
Enable verbose output - if supported - including the build commands to be executed
Pass remaining options to the native tool

subcommands.description: Project binary directory to install. This is required and must be first

options.description: For multi-configuration generators
Component-based install. Only install component specified
Default directory install permissions
Override the installation prefix
Strip before installing
Enable verbose output

subcommands.name: --open
subcommands.description: Open the generated project in the associated application. This is only supported by some generators

subcommands.name: -P
subcommands.description: Process the given cmake file as a script written in the CMake language. No configure or generate step is performed and the cache is not modified. If variables are defined using -D, this must be done before the -P argument

subcommands.name: -E
subcommands.description: CMake provides builtin command-line tools through the signature

subcommands.name: capabilities
subcommands.description: Report cmake capabilities in JSON format. The output is a JSON object with the following keys

subcommands.name: cat
subcommands.description: Concatenate files and print on the standard output

subcommands.name: chdir
subcommands.description: Change the current working directory and run a command

subcommands.name: compare_files
subcommands.description: Check if file1 is the same as file2. If fails are the same, then returns 0, if not returns 1. In case of invalid arguments, it returns 2

options.description: Implies line-wise comparison and ignores LF/CRLF differences

subcommands.name: copy
subcommands.description: Copy files to <destination> (either file or directory). If multiple files are specified, the <destination> must be directory and it must exist. Wildcards are not supported. copy does follow symlinks. That means it does not copy symlinks, but the files or directories it point to

subcommands.name: copy_directory
subcommands.description: Copy content of <dir>... directories to <destination> directory. If <destination> directory does not exist it will be created. copy_directory does follow symlinks

subcommands.name: copy_if_different
subcommands.description: Copy files to <destination> (either file or directory) if they have changed. If multiple files are specified, the <destination> must be directory and it must exist. copy_if_different does follow symlinks

subcommands.name: create_symlink
subcommands.description: Create a symbolic link <new> naming <old>

subcommands.name: create_hardlink
subcommands.description: Create a hard link <new> naming <old>

subcommands.name: echo
subcommands.description: Displays arguments as text

subcommands.name: echo_append
subcommands.description: Displays arguments as text but no new line

subcommands.name: env
subcommands.description: Run command in a modified environment

subcommands.name: environment
subcommands.description: Display the current environment variables

subcommands.name: false
subcommands.description: Do nothing, with an exit code of 1

subcommands.name: make_directory
subcommands.description: Create <dir> directories. If necessary, create parent directories too. If a directory already exists it will be silently ignored

subcommands.name: md5sum
subcommands.description: Create MD5 checksum of files in md5sum compatible format

subcommands.name: sha1sum
subcommands.description: Create SHA1 checksum of files in sha1sum compatible format

subcommands.name: sha224sum
subcommands.description: Create SHA224 checksum of files in sha224sum compatible format

subcommands.name: sha226sum
subcommands.description: Create SHA226 checksum of files in sha226sum compatible format

subcommands.name: sha384sum
subcommands.description: Create SHA384 checksum of files in sha384sum compatible format

subcommands.name: sha512sum
subcommands.description: Create SHA512 checksum of files in sha512sum compatible format

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.description: Remove the file(s). The planned behavior was that if any of the listed files already do not exist, the command returns a non-zero exit code, but no message is logged

options.description: The -f option changes the behavior to return a zero exit code (i.e. success) in such situations instead. remove does not follow symlinks. That means it remove only symlinks and not files it point to

subcommands.name: remove_directory
subcommands.description: Remove <dir> directories and their contents. If a directory does not exist it will be silently ignored. If <dir> is a symlink to a directory, just the symlink will be removed. Use rm instead

subcommands.name: rm
subcommands.description: Remove the files <file> or directories dir

options.description: Use -r or -R to remove directories and their contents recursively. If any of the listed files/directories do not exist, the command returns a non-zero exit code, but no message is logged
The -f option changes the behavior to return a zero exit code (i.e. success) in such situations instead

subcommands.name: server
subcommands.description: Launch cmake-server(7) mode

subcommands.name: sleep
subcommands.description: Sleep for given number of seconds

List archive contents. The <pathname>... argument could be used to list only selected files or directories
Produce verbose output
Compress the resulting archive with gzip
Compress the resulting archive with bzip2
Compress the resulting archive with XZ
Compress the resulting archive with Zstandard
Read file names from the given file, one per line. Blank lines are ignored. Lines may not start in - except for --add-file=<name> to add files whose names start in -
Specify the format of the archive to be created
Specify modification time recorded in tarball entries
Stop interpreting options and treat all remaining arguments as file names, even if they start with -

subcommands.name: time
subcommands.description: Run command and display elapsed time

subcommands.name: touch
subcommands.description: Creates <file> if file do not exist. If <file> exists, it is changing <file> access and modification times

subcommands.name: touch_nocreate
subcommands.description: Touch a file if it exists but do not create it. If a file does not exist it will be silently ignored

subcommands.name: true
subcommands.description: Do nothing, with an exit code of 0
